levels.name: Pre-Intentional
levels.descriptor: Behaviour reflects internal states (comfort, discomfort, arousal) without any intent to communicate with another person.

levels.name: Intentional
levels.descriptor: Behaviour is intentional but not yet a deliberate signal — a caregiver interprets it, but the child does not yet direct it at anyone.

levels.name: Unconventional Communication
levels.descriptor: Clear pre-symbolic signals directed at another person — reaching, pulling, pushing, vocalising, facial expression.

levels.name: Conventional Communication
levels.descriptor: Socially accepted gestures directed at another person — pointing, nodding, shaking head, giving, showing.

levels.name: Concrete Symbols
levels.descriptor: Symbols that resemble their meaning — pictures, objects, or signs that look or feel like what they represent.

levels.name: Abstract Symbols
levels.descriptor: Symbols with no physical resemblance to their meaning — spoken words, printed words, or abstract signs.

levels.name: Language
levels.descriptor: Symbols combined by grammatical rules into original, multi-word statements.

purposes.name: Obtain
purposes.descriptor: Requesting a wanted object, action, or more of something.

purposes.name: Social
purposes.descriptor: Engaging another person for its own sake — greeting, showing off, seeking attention or comfort.

purposes.name: Information
purposes.descriptor: Commenting, labelling, asking, or sharing information about the world.
